title: Expiration of Vehicle Service Contracts
content:
**Expiry.** A service contract under Vehicle Service Contracts expires on the earlier of its expiration date and the day the odometer reaches its expiration odometer; it is then fully earned and never refunded. Extensions of the retail installment contract never extend the service contract.

When it expires, the service contract passes from active to expired, and its record shows the date coverage ended as its closed date. Expiry is recorded by the system when the expiration date or expiration odometer is reached.

**The two limits side by side**

| Reached first | Coverage ends |
|---|---|
| The expiration date | on the expiration date |
| The expiration odometer | on the day the odometer reaches the expiration odometer |

**Consequences of expiry**

- The contract is fully earned: an expired service contract is never refunded.
- An extension granted on the retail installment contract leaves the service contract's expiration date and expiration odometer where they were.

**Hypothetical cases**

- A contract with an expiration odometer of 84000 miles and an expiration date still eight months away expires on the day the odometer reaches 84000 miles.
- A contract whose expiration date arrives while the odometer is still 5000 miles short of the expiration odometer expires on the expiration date.
- A contract whose retail installment contract received a two-month extension still expires on its own expiration date or expiration odometer, whichever comes first.
